blocks.text: 分享

inlines.text: 分享

blocks.text: 我们已与四家独立评估机构签署协议——Apollo Research、METR、Transluce 和 Goodfire——开展第一阶段的嵌入式评估。随着 AI 能力快速提升、潜在风险不断增大，独立评估的公开报告能让人们更清楚地了解各实验室如何评估和管理这些风险。

inlines.text: 我们已与四家独立评估机构签署协议——Apollo Research、METR、Transluce 和 Goodfire——开展第一阶段的嵌入式评估。随着 AI 能力快速提升、潜在风险不断增大，独立评估的公开报告能让人们更清楚地了解各实验室如何评估和管理这些风险。

blocks.text: 嵌入式评估让独立专家在较长时间内深入接触实验室的内部模型和系统，评估模型对齐情况以及防护措施的有效性，尤其是在与我们的安全案例相关的方面。根据每项评估的具体需要，评估人员可以访问我们研究人员使用的一些内部资源，包括模型检查点、源代码、训练和评估数据、监控系统、技术文档，以及与负责相关工作的研究人员和工程师的讨论。这样的访问权限让评估人员掌握证据和背景信息，从而开展独立评估，并发现我们可能没有预料到的失效情况。

inlines.text: 嵌入式评估让独立专家在较长时间内深入接触实验室的内部模型和系统，评估模型对齐情况以及防护措施的有效性，尤其是在与我们的安全案例相关的方面。根据每项评估的具体需要，评估人员可以访问我们研究人员使用的一些内部资源，包括模型检查点、源代码、训练和评估数据、监控系统、技术文档，以及与负责相关工作的研究人员和工程师的讨论。这样的访问权限让评估人员掌握证据和背景信息，从而开展独立评估，并发现我们可能没有预料到的失效情况。

blocks.text: 我们的初步评估聚焦于模型在训练和内部使用期间的对齐与防护措施，是对我们安全案例的补充。这些评估建立在我们对第三方评估的优先事项和原则以及多年来与第三方评估机构合作的基础上，包括最近一次对我们内部监控系统⁠(在新窗口打开)的试点评估（获得了深入的内部访问权限），以及对Hugging Face 事件⁠(在新窗口打开)的调查。我们将利用所学到的经验，在未来几个月深化与独立专家的合作。这些工作也支持我们在《白宫超级智能协议》下作出的承诺，即同意对我们的安全控制措施进行独立评估。这些合作有助于在整个行业推动形成更强的独立评估和公开透明共同标准。

blocks.text: Apollo Research

inlines.text: Apollo Research

blocks.text: 在这次试点评估中，Apollo Research⁠(在新窗口打开)将评估模型是否会暗中违背开发者的意图行事，以及我们的防护措施能否检测到这种行为。评估将依据来自训练、安全测试和内部使用的证据。Apollo 将分两个阶段评估四项主张：

inlines.text: 在这次试点评估中，
Apollo Research⁠(在新窗口打开)
将评估模型是否会暗中违背开发者的意图行事，以及我们的防护措施能否检测到这种行为。评估将依据来自训练、安全测试和内部使用的证据。Apollo 将分两个阶段评估四项主张：
训练没有激励颠覆行为。
严格的评估和红队测试不会诱发颠覆行为。
模型在内部使用期间没有尝试过颠覆行为。
颠覆行为背后的推理过程可以被检测到。

blocks.text: 在 Apollo 评估的第一阶段，我们将提供选定公开模型和未发布模型及训练检查点的访问权限、相关训练数据和评估结果、训练干预记录、监控系统和被标记的行为，以及能够提供背景信息的研究人员，并提供开展独立测试所需的工具和算力。

inlines.text: 在 Apollo 评估的第一阶段，我们将提供选定公开模型和未发布模型及训练检查点的访问权限、相关训练数据和评估结果、训练干预记录、监控系统和被标记的行为，以及能够提供背景信息的研究人员，并提供开展独立测试所需的工具和算力。

blocks.text: Goodfire

inlines.text: Goodfire

blocks.text: Goodfire⁠(在新窗口打开)将派驻可解释性研究人员，并使用 Goodfire 平台分析模型内部结构。其评估的主要目标是训练运行监控、调试和对齐。评估的主要受众是 OpenAI 内部研究人员，他们将利用评估发现来改进安全性。Goodfire 还将在合作推进过程中公开发布经验教训和评估发现。

inlines.text: Goodfire⁠(在新窗口打开)

blocks.text: Transluce

inlines.text: Transluce

blocks.text: Transluce⁠（在新窗口打开） 将对我们训练后对齐评估做一次初步评估，考察其质量和覆盖范围。初步评估阶段，我们将向 Transluce 开放部分公开模型和未发布模型、我们的训练后对齐评估及相关结果、支撑模型行为的数据和安全论证文档，并提供可说明背景的研究人员，以及开展独立测试所需的工具和算力。

blocks.text: OpenAI 与 Transluce 还计划在 2027 年初开展一次约八周的后续评估，届时将开放更多模型、更深入地访问我们的对齐评估，并提供评估结果如何影响模型发布决策的信息。

blocks.text: 嵌入式评估的协议

inlines.text: 嵌入式评估的协议

blocks.text: 我们参考评估方的意见，制定了一套协议和流程，在深度访问与安全、保密、监督以及评估的独立性和完整性之间取得平衡。我们公开这些内容，是为了说明我们将如何与嵌入式评估方合作，并推动关于嵌入式评估规范的讨论——这一领域目前尚无统一标准。随着我们对如何最好地开展这类评估有了更多认识，这些协议和流程预计也需要不断演进。尤其在嵌入式评估的早期阶段，我们预计会遇到技术访问难题、空间限制、不断变化的安全协议以及其他意外问题。我们希望与嵌入式评估方协作应对这些挑战，并分享经验教训。

blocks.text: 范围界定与迭代

inlines.text: 范围界定与迭代

blocks.text: 每次合作都从商定评估范围开始，并确定开展严格评估所需的访问权限、资源和安全安排。有些评估针对具体的安全主张；另一些则给评估方留出空间，在既定系统或训练运行内发现意料之外的失效模式。无论哪种情况，评估方都需要自由地循证据推进、改进方法，并在发现结果支持时提出进一步评估。我们还建立了流程，在评估推进过程中处理额外的访问需求。当直接访问可能暴露我们最敏感的 IP（例如模型权重或架构）时，我们会考虑替代方案，包括让评估方与 OpenAI 研究人员配对开展分析。

blocks.text: 安全、现场的环境

inlines.text: 安全、现场的环境

blocks.text: 需要接触敏感机密信息的评估人员将在 OpenAI 办公场所现场工作，并获得 OpenAI 设备来开展工作。主要目的是保护其所接触信息的安全。现场工作也让评估人员有机会与专职人员交流，这些人员可以帮助他们熟悉访问权限，并为其评估提供背景信息。我们还期望我们的嵌入式评估人员在开展实验和评估时，至少遵循与 OpenAI 员工3相同的安全标准。

blocks.text: 监督与争议解决

inlines.text: 监督与争议解决

blocks.text: 我们的安全与安保委员会（SSC）是 OpenAI 基金会董事会的独立监督委员会，将能够了解嵌入式评估的情况，并有权在评估开始前、进行中和结束时行使监督职责。他们将收到未经删减的报告，评估人员和 SSC 在评估期间可以相互沟通，包括私下沟通。OpenAI 与任何评估方之间的分歧将上报至安全咨询小组和 OpenAI 高管，后者将在规定期限内解决，分歧一经上报，SSC 会立即收到通知。如果分歧仍未解决，该事项将提交 SSC 裁决。

blocks.text: 员工讨论与证明

inlines.text: 员工讨论与证明

blocks.text: 与员工讨论有助于评估人员理解内部信息和工作背景。OpenAI 将授权并指导可接受评估人员访谈的员工，评估人员也可根据需要请求增加访谈对象。为鼓励坦诚交流并保护员工隐私，这些讨论不做记录，这意味着讨论内容可用于评估，但不得公开发表或归因于具体员工。通过单独的证明渠道，评估人员可以请求 OpenAI 出具证明，以核实、更正或澄清他们在与员工交谈中了解到的情况。这些证明不归因于个人，也不旨在描述个人观点。评估人员可以公开发表 OpenAI 予以证明的陈述，或披露 OpenAI 拒绝证明某项陈述。

inlines.text: 展望未来

blocks.text: 这些评估为我们持续推进的对齐与安全工作带来了独立视角。公开报告评估发现，会让这项工作更加透明，也能让人更放心地了解风险是如何被识别和应对的。我们预计首阶段的评估将逐步发展为长期、稳定、常驻式的合作，持续提供第三方安全信号，并就我们最关键的安全主张和安全论证提出改进建议。

blocks.text: 未来几个月，我们将支持围绕更广泛安全问题的外部评估。我们也在探索未来的常驻式评估，考察我们对安全框架的遵守情况，以及组织文化和流程。我们致力于扩大这项工作，并帮助建设维持这项工作所需的能力和共同标准。

blocks.text: We have signed agreements with four independent assessors—Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire—for our first phase of embedded assessments. As AI capabilities advance rapidly and the potential risks grow, public reporting from independent assessments can give people a clearer view of how labs are evaluating and managing those risks.

inlines.text: We have signed agreements with four independent assessors—Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire—for our first phase of embedded assessments. As AI capabilities advance rapidly and the potential risks grow, public reporting from independent assessments can give people a clearer view of how labs are evaluating and managing those risks.

blocks.text: Embedded assessments give independent experts deep access to a lab’s internal models and systems to assess model alignment and the effectiveness of safeguards over an extended period of time, especially where relevant to our safety cases. Based on what each evaluation needs, assessors receive access to some of the same internal resources our researchers use, including model checkpoints, source code, training and evaluation data, monitoring systems, technical documentation, and discussions with the researchers and engineers responsible for the work. This access gives assessors the evidence and context to pursue independent evaluations and uncover failures we may not have anticipated.

blocks.text: Our initial assessments focus on alignment and safeguards for models during training and internal use, complementing our safety cases. They build on our priorities and principles for third party assessments and years of work with third party evaluators, including a recent pilot assessment of our internal monitoring systems⁠(opens in a new window) with deep internal access and an investigation of the Hugging Face incident⁠(opens in a new window). We’ll use what we learn to deepen our work with independent experts in the coming months. These efforts also support our commitments under the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, where we agreed to independent assessments of our safety controls. These collaborations can contribute to stronger shared standards for independent assessment and public transparency across the industry.

Apollo Research⁠(opens in a new window)

Goodfire will also publish learnings and findings as the collaboration progresses.

blocks.text: Protocols for embedded assessments

inlines.text: Protocols for embedded assessments

blocks.text: We’ve developed protocols and processes with input from the assessors to balance deep access with security, confidentiality, oversight, and the independence and integrity of assessments. We are sharing them to shed light on how we will work with embedded assessors, and to advance discussion about norms for embedded assessments, which have yet to be standardized. We expect that these will need to evolve as we learn more about how to best conduct these assessments. Especially in the early stages of embedded assessments, we expect technical access challenges, space constraints, evolving security protocols, and other unexpected issues to arise. We hope to work through these challenges collaboratively with our embedded assessors and share lessons learned.

blocks.text: Scoping and iteration

inlines.text: Scoping and iteration

blocks.text: Each engagement begins with an agreed scope and the access, resources, and safety arrangements needed to conduct a rigorous assessment. Some assessments test specific safety claims; others give assessors room to discover unexpected failure modes within a defined system or training run. In both cases, assessors need the freedom to follow evidence, refine their methods, and propose further assessments when findings warrant it. We also have a process for addressing additional access needs as assessments develop. When direct access could expose our most sensitive IP, such as model weights or architecture, we will consider alternatives, including pairing assessors with OpenAI researchers to run analyses.

blocks.text: A secure, on-site environment

inlines.text: A secure, on-site environment

blocks.text: Assessors who need access to sensitive confidential information will work on site at OpenAI offices and be provided OpenAI devices to conduct their work. The primary purpose is to protect the security of the information they access. Working onsite also gives assessors the opportunity to engage with dedicated staff who can help them navigate their access and provide context for their assessments. We also expect our embedded assessors to follow at minimum3 the same security standards as OpenAI employees when running experiments and evaluations.

blocks.text: Oversight and dispute resolution

inlines.text: Oversight and dispute resolution

blocks.text: Our Safety and Security Committee (SSC), an independent oversight committee of the OpenAI Foundation’s Board, will have visibility into the embedded assessment and the ability to exercise their oversight responsibilities before, during, and at their conclusion. They will receive unredacted reports, and both the assessors and the SSC will be able to speak with each other during the assessment, including privately. Disagreements among OpenAI and any evaluator will be escalated to the Safety Advisory Group and OpenAI executives, who will have a specified time period to resolve them, and the SSC will be notified of any such disagreements promptly when escalated. If a disagreement remains, the matter will be referred to the SSC for resolution.

blocks.text: Employee discussions and attestation

inlines.text: Employee discussions and attestation

blocks.text: Discussions with employees help assessors understand internal information and the context behind the work. OpenAI will authorize and provide guidance to staff members who can speak to assessors, and assessors may request additional staff to speak with as needed. To encourage open, candid conversations and protect the privacy of our staff, these discussions are off the record, meaning that they can inform the assessments but cannot be published or attributed to employees. Through a separate attestation pathway, assessors can request OpenAI-attested statements verifying, correcting, or clarifying something they learned in conversation with employees. These statements are not attributed to individuals or intended to characterize individual views. Assessors may publish statements that OpenAI attests to, or disclose that OpenAI declined to attest to a statement.

blocks.text: Conflict disclosures & cool off periods

inlines.text: Conflict disclosures & cool off periods

blocks.text: Managing conflicts of interest clearly and transparently—including those involving personal relationships, financial interests4, and other issues—is important to the integrity and independence of evaluations. Cool-off periods5 also need to be designed carefully, so assessors can work responsibly across labs while handling competitive information sensitively. We are working with our assessors to develop clear processes for both conflicts and cool-off periods, including allowing for flexibility in mitigations and transparency in decisions to request recusal.

blocks.text: Publication and responsible disclosure periods

inlines.text: Publication and responsible disclosure periods

blocks.text: Assessors maintain independence in publishing their assessments, but we will retain the right to redact confidential information, consistent with our previous third-party engagements. We may also request responsible disclosure delays to allow time to act on findings that could pose security or safety risks and remediate issues that remain.

blocks.text: Public reporting will help people understand the findings and their limitations, while more detailed confidential reports give oversight bodies the evidence they need to act. We want these assessments to improve how we identify and address risks, and give the public a clearer basis for judging our safety work.

blocks.text: Looking ahead

inlines.text: Looking ahead

blocks.text: These assessments bring an independent perspective to our ongoing alignment and safety work. Public reporting on their findings will make that work more transparent and provide greater assurance about how risks are being identified and addressed. We expect this first phase of assessments to lead to longer-term, consistent embedded engagements over time that can continuously provide third party safety signals and recommended improvements on our most load bearing safety claims and safety cases.

blocks.text: We’ll continue working with multiple independent third parties to help build a healthy assessment ecosystem with diverse expertise and approaches. Some investigations need sustained, on-site work with sensitive systems; others primarily evaluate deployed or soon to be deployed models or review public documentation.

blocks.text: In the coming months, we’ll support external assessments across a broader range of safety questions. We are also exploring future embedded assessments that would examine compliance with our safety frameworks, as well as our organizational culture and processes. We are committed to expanding this work and helping build the capacity and shared standards needed to sustain it.
